findings.source_quote: divitiae suae eos pusillum obscuraverunt a veritate atque obfuscaverunt
findings.english_quote: Their riches have somewhat obscured and clouded their view of the truth.
findings.issue: The Latin makes the people themselves the object of the darkening and describes their separation from truth. Introducing “their view” narrows this to perception, rather than preserving the source's broader assertion about their condition.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “Their riches have darkened them a little with respect to the truth and clouded them.” Review the final wording afresh to preserve both the personal object and the relation to truth without adding a merely perceptual limitation.

findings.source_quote: hi autem omnes candidi inventi sunt, qui crediderunt et qui credituri sunt
findings.english_quote: The cited Vulgata manuscripts have iuvenes, “young.”
findings.issue: The supplied report identifies cited L₁ as reading iuvenes and reports L₂/Palatina support for inventi. The unqualified plural “manuscripts” overstates the supplied evidence for iuvenes and obscures that distinction.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this sentence with: “The supplied project report identifies the cited L₁ reading as iuvenes, ‘young,’ and reports L₂/Palatina support for inventi.” Retain the disclosed working correction and the warning that Amherst does not certify it.

findings.source_quote: ἔγνω γὰρ ὅτι, ἐὰν ἀπέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν [τοῦ πύργου] οἱ λίθοι οὗτοι, διαμενοῦσι λαμπροί, καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν μελανήσει.
findings.english_quote: He knew these stones would stay bright in the building. Not one would turn black.
findings.issue: The explicit condition concerning the stones' entry into the building is omitted. The source states what he knew would happen if they entered; the simplified text replaces that conditional construction with an unqualified prediction.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “He knew that if these stones went into the building, they would stay bright. Not one of them would turn black.” Review this replacement directly against the Greek before adoption.

findings.source_quote: divitiae suae eos pusillum obscuraverunt a veritate atque obfuscaverunt
findings.english_quote: Their riches somewhat clouded their view of the truth.
findings.issue: As independently compared with the Latin, this substitutes the people's “view” for the people themselves and reduces their darkening away from truth to a perceptual problem. The single expression also makes the source's paired darkening/clouding language less explicit.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “Their riches had darkened and clouded them a little with respect to the truth.” Review the final wording for readable preservation of the people as the affected object and of their relation to truth.

findings.source_quote: hi autem omnes candidi inventi sunt, qui crediderunt et qui credituri sunt
findings.english_quote: The cited Vulgata manuscripts have iuvenes, “young.”
findings.issue: The supplied evidence attributes iuvenes specifically to cited L₁, while reporting L₂/Palatina support for inventi. This plural statement claims broader manuscript support than the supplied report establishes.
findings.suggested_revision: Identify the reported witnesses separately: cited L₁ has iuvenes according to the supplied report; inventi is the working correction with reported L₂/Palatina support. Do not change the selected working reading merely because the alternative exists.

findings.source_quote: ideo ergo pusillum circumcisi sunt et positi sunt in structuram turris huius.
findings.english_quote: Retain name-bearing suffering, healing and gift language, infant innocence, stone/root/wealth imagery and all critical footnotes without turning editorial supply into unanimous manuscript text.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims retention of name-bearing suffering, healing, gift language, and infant innocence, none of which occurs in this selected unit. This is inaccurate unit-specific audit documentation, although the stone/root/wealth imagery and footnote disclosure do belong here.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the unrelated material and describe only the simplifications actually made in this unit, including preservation of its conditional statement, innocence language, stone/root/wealth imagery, and textual uncertainties.

summary: Both editions require targeted revisions. They otherwise preserve the section's major assertions, necessity, negations, speaker attribution, and disclosed Greek-to-Latin boundary. The selected inventi correction and dagger-marked Latin crux should remain provisionally translated with their disclosures; the bounded Amherst report does not warrant replacing the continuous Latin or certifying its uncertain wording. This review evaluates the supplied source and attributed reports, not unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation. All suggested replacements require fresh review.
